Attached is our initial CAIQ annotation for HelixBank along with an artifact manifest that maps each CSA control to the suggested evidence items and the Redwood owners. Highlights:
- Spreadsheet: HelixBank_CAIQ_annotated.xlsx — yellow rows indicate controls with missing evidence; green are complete.
- Manifest: artifact_manifest.csv — canonical filenames and preferred locations for uploads.

1) You confirm scope by EOD Wed (3/7).
2) If ok, we schedule a 45-minute walkthrough the week of 3/13 to review high-priority controls and sampling approach.
3) Helix provides a drop date for initial evidence (we recommend a 2-week window).

Attachments: HelixBank_CAIQ_annotated.xlsx (CAIQ crosswalk), artifact_manifest.csv (file manifest).

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if easier.

Thanks, Kimberly — and thanks for the clear manifest. Quick notes from our side:

- We need a brief extension to collect some of the runtime artifacts (logs and retention configs) — internal change freeze this week. Can we aim for an initial drop by 3/20 instead of 3/13?
- For scope: HelixBank wants tenant-level coverage for authentication, key management, and telemetry; workload-level for transaction-processing lanes only. Hope that distinction is ok.
- Are the runtime logs you reference the same as 'Inference runtime telemetry' in section CC6? If yes, we will require a sample format and the retention window you recommend.

On quoting your original:
> Attached is our initial CAIQ annotation for HelixBank along with an artifact manifest...

I'll loop in our internal infra owner if we need deeper access. Also, can Redwood provide an example of a minimal evidence bundle for a high-priority control (e.g., identity lifecycle)? That will help us prioritize.

Hi Aisha — thanks for the scope clarification, that helps. To answer your questions:

1) "Inference runtime telemetry" in CC6 maps to the same artifact set we referenced in the manifest (logs, kv-cache traces, audit events). We can provide a 72-hour sampled export in CSV/JSON format.

2) Minimal evidence bundle (example for identity lifecycle control):
   - Identity lifecycle policy doc (pdf) — signed and dated
   - IAM role listing exported from cloud console (csv) — include last modified timestamps
   - Access review cadence notes (meeting minutes) or screenshots of attestations
   - Sample audit log lines showing provisioning/deprovisioning events (anonymized)

3) We have a short guidance PDF attached: log_sample_instructions.pdf that shows the exact CSV schema we accept. If Helix wants, Redwood can perform the export (read-only role) under an NDA; otherwise you can upload to the Drive link below.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
- By 3/10: Helix confirms final scope and authorized upload accounts.
- By 3/20: Helix uploads initial sample bundle (logs + top 10 control artifacts).
- 3/22–3/24: Redwood performs review and calls out gaps; schedule walkthroughs for remaining items.

Attachments: log_sample_instructions.pdf (pdf, 48 KB).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
